meta: Dramas like What's Wrong with Secretary Kim: six office romances with the same chemistry and better plots.
standfirst: A narcissist chief executive, the secretary who has run his life for nine years, and a resignation letter that starts the whole thing. What people came for is the two of them in a room being funny at each other, and the plot underneath is almost entirely optional. These six deliver that dynamic, and we say where each one has more or less story attached.

picks.why: The same actress, the same office, a better back half. Park Min Young again, opposite a new boss who finds out something embarrassing about her private life and decides to protect it. Identical pleasure: two competent adults in a workplace, together early, staying together, with the comedy coming from the gap between their public and private selves. Difference: no amnesia, no childhood trauma reveal, and the highest rewatch scores of any romance in this catalog.

The purest version of the boss-employee joke. A blind date under a false identity where the man on the other side is the chief executive, played entirely for farce and moving at twice the speed. Same appetite for a live-action cartoon and the same willingness to let two leads carry everything. Difference: twelve episodes rather than sixteen, so it never has to invent a second act.

Cold professional, warm woman, same shape. An actress placed as a secretary in a law firm, and a lawyer who has no idea how to be around her. It hits the exact same beats and Lee Dong Wook plays stiffness better than almost anyone. Difference: it has even less plot, and the middle stretch sags harder, with the per-episode ratings falling under seven before recovering.

The chaebol heir and the employee, at hotel scale. Same power gap, same glossy corporate setting, same structure of a man learning to be a person because one member of staff will not flatter him. Difference: it is thinner even than this one, and it is worse at the workplace half, treating the hotel as wallpaper rather than as a job.

If you want the same leads-first comedy with an actual plot bolted on. Ji Chang Wook and Nam Ji Hyun in a law office, bickering their way into a relationship while a murder case runs in parallel. The romance half is as good as this one's. Difference: the other half is a serial-killer thriller, so the tone lurches in a way Secretary Kim never does.

The same warmth, at a much lower income bracket. Two friends of twenty years who finally get together, and a show that is genuinely interested in the part after they do. Same easy chemistry, same comic rhythm. Difference: nobody here is rich, the workplace is a humiliation rather than a status symbol, and the show has real things on its mind.

against.title: Crash Landing on You
against.why: The default recommendation for anybody who liked one popular romance, and it shares almost nothing with this. Crash Landing on You is a separation melodrama with a body count and a political plot. Secretary Kim has no jeopardy at all, and that is the entire product.

against.title: Strong Woman Do Bong Soon
against.why: Paired because both are 2017 to 2018 office romcoms with a chaebol lead. But that one welds its comedy to a kidnapping plot and a cartoon villain, so half its runtime is spent somewhere you did not want to go. This one never leaves the office.

against.title: Something in the Rain
against.why: Suggested as the grown-up version of the same office romance, which is exactly backwards. It is a slow, quiet, deeply unhappy film about family pressure and a workplace that punishes women. Watch it for what it is, not as a replacement for something you enjoyed because it was easy.
